shortBackstory: Ancient World Boss: Leviathan of the First Flood is a non-playable Ancient World Boss whose origin makes Storm-Oath Covenant visible as living battlefield danger.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Ancient World Boss: Leviathan of the First Flood slept below pre-Gate waters until multiple scars aligned like a wound-map. It is not a faction citizen and should never read like a recruitable Titan. Its existence proves that the Gate crisis produces consequences, predators, remnants, and catastrophes beyond civilized armies.

chapters.title: Lore Function
chapters.text: As a Ancient World Boss from Pre-Gate Mythic Deep, Ancient carries a specific warning into the story: A catastrophic primordial beast awakened when multiple Gate scars align beneath ancient waters. It is a campaign-scale threat, not a faction unit. This makes the creature useful as canon pressure, not random enemy dressing.

chapters.title: Battlefield Behavior
chapters.text: On the map, Ancient supports its lore through behavior: Campaign boss encounter that transforms terrain each phase. Its abilities — Flood the Map, Temple Chain Drag, Primordial Roar — should feel like the environment and story acting through a threat body.

chapters.title: Campaign Tie
chapters.text: In Storm-Oath Covenant, Ancient connects to the raid-scale omen beneath future covenant shield objectives. Encounter designers can place it where the player needs to feel what the Gate has damaged: memory, structure, instinct, oath, water, stone, or command.

chapters.title: Visual / Reading Rule
chapters.text: The creature page must preserve the distinction between Titans, NPCs, and non-playable threats. Ancient can be studied under Creatures and Backstories, but its profile should reinforce danger, not companionship.

developmentStatus: Readable creature profile integrated into dashboard threat pages.
